1045	Run `pose delegate resume <run>` (`--dry-run` previews it; repeating it returns the recorded continuation) to continue with the same agent, captured session, brief digest, sealed commit and reconstructed checkout digest. Every run of an attempt recreates its sealed checkout at the same path under the dispatcher's temporary directory, so the resumed session finds the checkout it worked in; resume from a shell with the same `TMPDIR`. When that directory is still there (an unfinished cleanup, or another process holding the path), resume refuses before it starts: remove the directory, then resume. Resume uses the original attempt and does not spend another attempt quota. The default maximum is three resumes and 60 minutes of accumulated wall-clock; configure `resume.max_resumes`/`max_wall_time` to change these bounds. Policy changes, changed inputs, lost or rewritten predecessors, terminal predecessors and spent budgets refuse. An immutable predecessor claim permits only one continuation; repeated requests return the recorded result or expose its pending reservation without launching another process. A lost host before a result is published remains explicit incomplete evidence; this is not automatic recovery without a captured interrupted record.

907	The sandboxed Claude review profile that pose-dist qualified for its own reviews uses safe/restricted mode, Read/Grep/Glob/Bash only, mandatory shell sandboxing (`failIfUnavailable:true`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands:false`), and a read-only sealed source tree. Both fresh and resumed wrappers require bubblewrap, socat and jq on Linux (jq remains required on macOS), with installation advice on refusal. Go cache/temp writes go to private operation-owned scratch outside the checkout; the existing module cache is read, and unavailable downloads/tests that write into source can fail. The profile instructs the reviewer to run `go clean -cache` as its final Bash command inside the sandbox; the engine independently retains incomplete cleanup as a failed run under its unchanged limits. Never clean an adapter-controlled cache outside the sandbox: a test can replace its path with a symlink. This qualifies Claude's shell subprocess boundary, not isolation of the trusted Claude executable or arbitrary credential reads. Checkout integrity checks still apply. Installing engine code does not adopt the profile in another instance; copy and qualify its explicit policy block before use. The wrapper also denies the resolved physical Git common directory, because Claude auto-allows it for worktrees. For this opt-in profile, POSE prepares only empty `.claude/.cc-writes` directories at the disposable checkout root and declared components before taking its integrity snapshot; added files and all later mutations still fail. Final sandboxed cleanup includes leftover `go-build*` directories directly under GOTMPDIR after all jobs finish.

## What did not run
- **Tests and diff:** I ran no `go test`, `go vet` or `git diff`. I haven't confirmed the mutation claims, and I took the change list from the brief.
- **Pose tools:** `artifact-check` and `review-check` failed at sandbox start, and I didn't run the others. `artifact-check` is required and has no sealed substitute, so the conclusion preflight may refuse this draft.
- **Draft check:** `review draft-check` needs Bash, so the block below is unchecked.
- **Cleanup:** `go clean -cache` and the `go-build*` removal both failed, so cleanup did not happen. I started no builds or background jobs.
- **Sealed evidence:** where a criterion or `validate` is marked passed, it cites sealed results that I did not rerun.

## Findings

| ID | Severity | Disposition | Location | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N7 | low | blocker | `POSE.md:1045` | The manual says that when the directory remains because of an unfinished cleanup, you can remove it and resume. `PlanReviewResume` refuses a predecessor with incomplete cleanup first (`review_run_continuity.go:405-407`), so removing the directory doesn't restore resume. The same claim is in the other three manual copies, the spec's technical risks (line 79) and the error text (`review_dispatch.go:2082`). |
| N6 | low | follow-up | `delegation_handoff.go:329` | `PlanReviewHandoff` never calls `reviewRunRuntimeDirFree`. With a leftover or foreign directory, a handoff claims the predecessor (`review_dispatch.go:746`) and then fails at `:809`. The interrupted run can then no longer be resumed. Random names ruled out this collision before. R3's wording covers only resume. |
| N8 | low | follow-up | `review_run_continuity.go:431` | The claim lookup (`:413`) and the directory check are not atomic. A concurrent winner can claim and create the directory between them. The loser is then told to remove a directory that a live run is using, instead of getting "pending". The window is narrow, and I did not reproduce it. |
| N9 | low | follow-up | `.pose/indexes/validation-matrix.json:2639` | The continuity integration check runs `-run RunContinuity`, which selects neither new test. The matrix has no pattern naming them, so I rely on the full unit suite for R1–R3. |
| N10 | low | follow-up | `review_run_runtime_dir_test.go:14` | The test isolates itself with `TMPDIR`, which Windows ignores. With its fixed attempt id it would use the real temp directory, and could leave a link there that fails later runs. |

On the lead's three questions, from reading:
- **Sharing or following:** `os.Mkdir` refuses an existing path, including a link.
- **Cleanup:** the normal path removes the worktree, its Git registration and the runtime directory.
- **Runs without an attempt:** they still get a random name.

I found no reason to dispute L1–L3.

| N7 | low | blocker | `POSE.md:1045` | The manual says that when the directory remains because of an unfinished cleanup, you can remove it and resume. `PlanReviewResume` refuses a predecessor with incomplete cleanup first (`review_run_continuity.go:405-407`), so removing the directory doesn't restore resume. The same claim is in the other three manual copies, the spec's technical risks (line 79) and the error text (`review_dispatch.go:2082`). |
| N6 | low | follow-up | `delegation_handoff.go:329` | `PlanReviewHandoff` never calls `reviewRunRuntimeDirFree`. With a leftover or foreign directory, a handoff claims the predecessor (`review_dispatch.go:746`) and then fails at `:809`. The interrupted run can then no longer be resumed. Random names ruled out this collision before. R3's wording covers only resume. |
| N8 | low | follow-up | `review_run_continuity.go:431` | The claim lookup (`:413`) and the directory check are not atomic. A concurrent winner can claim and create the directory between them. The loser is then told to remove a directory that a live run is using, instead of getting "pending". The window is narrow, and I did not reproduce it. |
| N9 | low | follow-up | `.pose/indexes/validation-matrix.json:2639` | The continuity integration check runs `-run RunContinuity`, which selects neither new test. The matrix has no pattern naming them, so I rely on the full unit suite for R1–R3. |
| N10 | low | follow-up | `review_run_runtime_dir_test.go:14` | The test isolates itself with `TMPDIR`, which Windows ignores. With its fixed attempt id it would use the real temp directory, and could leave a link there that fails later runs. |
